description: non-commutative aten.matmul: operands swapped from (n0, n1) to (n1, n0).
note: KEY CASE. aten.matmul is non-commutative, so swapping operands changes the result. The diff MUST classify n2 as modified. A naive algorithm that sorts inputs would produce an identical signature and miss this (a silent diff bug). This is why the contract stores inputs as an ordered sequence (ADR-024) and the signature preserves operand order for non-commutative ops. This is the must-detect half of the operand-order regression guarantee.
